security_audit.summary: The review confirmed documented RunComfy CLI execution, a POST to the RunComfy Model API, and local RunComfy token storage. Most other detections are Markdown formatting, example placeholders, REST path abbreviations, or sample prompts with no execution behavior. No prompt injection or covert data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before running RunComfy CLI commands. Keep prompt and image inputs structured, and avoid shell interpolation.
Tell users that prompts, image URLs, and bearer tokens are sent to RunComfy. Warn against submitting sensitive private assets.
Keep the token file owner-only, never print it, and document RUNCOMFY_TOKEN as the preferred CI option.

content.user_title: Generate GPT Image 2 Assets on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Teams need accurate image prompts, edits, and RunComfy settings for GPT Image 2. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through model selection, commands, and safe output handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose GPT Image 2 instead of Flux 2, Nano Banana Pro, or Seedream.
Shows RunComfy CLI usage for text-to-image and image edit endpoints.
Documents supported image sizes, edit inputs, multi-reference images, and output handling.
Provides prompt patterns for embedded text, composition, and preservation edits.
Describes RunComfy authentication, token storage, outbound endpoints, download behavior, and exit codes.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a RunComfy account or token.
Uses RunComfy, not a direct OpenAI API connection.
Text-to-image supports only three fixed sizes; edit also supports auto sizing.
Reference images must be public HTTPS URLs and may be fetched by the model server.

use_cases.title: Create product launch imagery
use_cases.description: Produce product hero images with concise labels, controlled lighting, and supported RunComfy image sizes.

use_cases.title: Prepare precise image edits
use_cases.description: Rewrite edit instructions so identity, framing, typography, and key objects stay stable across iterations.

use_cases.title: Automate model runs
use_cases.description: Plan RunComfy CLI usage, output handling, exit codes, and token setup for repeatable image workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple product image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 on RunComfy to create a square product hero image. Include the product, setting, lighting, and exact label text.

prompt_templates.title: Edit one reference image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the edit endpoint with one public reference image. Change only the background and preserve the subject, pose, face identity, and framing.

prompt_templates.title: Build localized ad variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three ad prompts for GPT Image 2. Keep the same composition and change only the quoted headline language in each version.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a multi-reference composite
prompt_templates.prompt: Use up to 10 public reference images. Assign each image a role, define what to preserve, and choose auto size unless framing must change.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks for a launch image with a short product label.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends GPT Image 2, selects a supported portrait size, and gives a concise prompt with exact label text.

output_examples.input: A designer provides two public reference images for a room composite.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares an edit instruction that assigns roles to image 1 and image 2, then preserves lighting and framing.

output_examples.input: A developer needs reliable automation behavior.
output_examples.output: The skill explains authentication, output folders, exit codes, polling, cancellation, and generated file downloads.

best_practices: Quote embedded text exactly and keep it short.
Change one visual attribute per edit iteration.
Use auto size for edits unless the frame must change.
anti_patterns: Do not combine conflicting instructions, such as no text and a required headline.
Do not submit private images unless RunComfy processing is acceptable.
Do not expect unsupported aspect ratios or long paragraphs of rendered text.

faq.question: What does this skill help generate?
faq.answer: It helps create and edit GPT Image 2 outputs through RunComfy, including product images, ads, signage, and mockups.

faq.question: Can it call OpenAI directly?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy Model API and requires a RunComfy account or token.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What image sizes are supported?
faq.answer: Text-to-image supports three fixed sizes. Edit supports those sizes plus auto sizing for preservation.

faq.question: Does it support multiple reference images?
faq.answer: Yes. The edit endpoint supports up to 10 public HTTPS reference image URLs.

faq.question: Does it store credentials?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI stores a local token after login. CI workflows can use RUNCOMFY_TOKEN instead.
